quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: My friend's parking the car, so I'll order for both of us: a cappuccino for me and an iced tea for her.
quests.hint: Two people, one speaker - both drinks belong to the same order.
quests.explanation: When you order for someone who isn't at the table yet, you simply name both items; 'for her' tells you who gets the second drink.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: She said she'd have the chicken wrap, and I'll just have the soup.
quests.hint: Reported speech still names a real choice, even though the speaker isn't the one eating it.
quests.explanation: 'She said she'd have X' passes along someone else's order secondhand. The item after 'have' goes on the order just like your own.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the guest's final order.
quests.prompt: Server: And for the gentleman? Customer: Oh, he'll have the burger - no, wait, the fish and chips. I'll take the Greek salad.
quests.hint: A correction is made about someone else's order, not the speaker's own.
quests.explanation: You can correct an order for another person exactly like your own; 'no, wait' cancels the burger and the fish and chips replaces it.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: We're a family of four: two kids' pizzas, a Caesar salad for my wife, and I'll have the lasagna.
quests.hint: Count the different dishes, not the number of people at the table.
quests.explanation: Family orders often repeat one item; 'two kids' pizzas' is still just one menu item to tap.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: For the little ones, chicken nuggets; for us, the family platter to share, and a pitcher of lemonade.
quests.correctAnswer: Pitcher of Lemonade, Chicken Nuggets, Family Platter
quests.hint: 'For the little ones' and 'for us' split the order between two groups.
quests.explanation: Splitting an order by group ('for the kids... for us') is a natural way to organize a family order.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: My husband and I will share the steak, and the kids want the mac and cheese - only one order, they'll split it.
quests.hint: Sharing changes how many portions are served, not which items are ordered.
quests.explanation: 'Share' and 'split' both mean one portion for several people - the item is still ordered only once.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Do you have a kids' menu? Great - my daughter will have the grilled cheese, and I'll have the club sandwich.
quests.hint: A question about the menu comes before the actual order.
quests.explanation: 'Do you have a kids' menu?' is the natural way to ask; kids' items are usually smaller portions at lower prices.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: She's only three, so could she have a small portion of pasta with the sauce on the side? And I'll have the chicken salad.
quests.hint: A detail about age explains the request - it isn't an item itself.
quests.explanation: Giving a child's age is a polite way to explain why you're asking for a smaller portion or a plainer preparation.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Could we get a plastic cup with a lid for my son, with milk in it? And an apple juice for me.
quests.hint: The cup is a container request; the drinks are what you tap.
quests.explanation: Requests like 'a cup with a lid' describe how a drink is served, not what the drink is.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: We're five people. Can we get two large pizzas - one pepperoni, one veggie - and a pitcher of soda?
quests.correctAnswer: Veggie Pizza, Pitcher of Soda, Pepperoni Pizza
quests.hint: 'One X, one Y' means two different pizzas, not the same one twice.
quests.explanation: When a group orders 'one of this, one of that,' each type is its own menu item, even though both are pizzas.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: We'll all have the lunch special - five with the salad and one with the soup instead.
quests.correctAnswer: Lunch Special with Salad, Lunch Special with Soup
quests.hint: The numbers tell you how many, but both versions still appear as separate items.
quests.explanation: Counts like 'five' and 'one' describe quantities; what you tap is each distinct version of the dish.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Could we get the sharing platters for the table - the meat one and the veggie one? Everybody will order drinks later.
quests.hint: 'Later' postpones the drinks, so nothing drink-related is ordered yet.
quests.explanation: Saying drinks will come later tells the server not to wait for them; only the platters are ordered now.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Ana's having the pasta, no cheese; Ben's the salmon; and I'll have the salad, dressing on the side.
quests.hint: Each name is attached to one dish - three people, three dishes.
quests.explanation: Listing an order by name ('Ana's having...') is a clear way to keep several people's choices separate.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Mine's the soup. My sister can't eat mushrooms, so hers is the chicken, not the mushroom risotto. And my dad wants the fish.
quests.hint: One dish is named only to say what was rejected.
quests.explanation: A dish mentioned as 'not the...' is a rejection, so it doesn't belong in the final order.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Everyone's got something different: Tom's having the beef tacos, Priya wants the same as Tom but with fish, and I'll go with the enchiladas.
quests.hint: 'The same as... but' builds one order out of another.
quests.explanation: 'The same but with X' is an efficient way to order a near-copy: keep the base dish, change one detail.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Two soups, one with bread and one without, and a salad we'll share.
quests.hint: 'One with, one without' means the bread only appears once.
quests.explanation: Bread goes to only one of the two soups, so it's ordered once; the salad is a shared item.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: I'll have the curry; my wife will have the same curry but mild; and could we get one naan for the table?
quests.hint: The second dish is built from the first, with a single change.
quests.explanation: Ordering 'the same but mild' creates a second, distinct menu item based on the first one.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: The kids are sharing one pizza, my husband's having the pasta, and I'm not that hungry - just a side salad for me.
quests.hint: The speaker's own order is the smallest one on the table.
quests.explanation: 'I'm not that hungry - just...' explains a smaller order and tells you the item that follows is deliberately light.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: My boss texted me her order: the Cobb salad with the dressing on the side and a sparkling water. I'll have the same.
quests.hint: 'The same' copies the whole order that was just read out.
quests.explanation: 'I'll have the same' repeats the order just mentioned - here, an order relayed from a text message for two people.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: She's in the restroom. Before she left she said the ravioli, so I'll order that, and I'll get the gnocchi.
quests.hint: One of the two dishes belongs to a person who isn't at the table right now.
quests.explanation: You can order on behalf of someone who stepped away, as long as you pass on exactly what they told you.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Server: Is your friend ready to order? Customer: She's still deciding, so I'll go first - the risotto and a lemonade - and she'll tell you when you come back.
quests.hint: Someone else's order is postponed, not included.
quests.explanation: Saying 'she'll tell you when you come back' means her order isn't part of what's placed now.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: My friend's vegetarian - is the vegetable lasagna meat-free? It is? Then she'll have that, and I'll have the meatball sub.
quests.hint: A question about a friend's diet leads to a choice for her, not for the speaker.
quests.explanation: Asking about a restriction on someone else's behalf is natural: name the person's need, then ask about the dish.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Server: The kitchen says the banana bread is nut-free. Customer: Thank you - one for my son, then, and a coffee for me.
quests.hint: The order only happens after the kitchen's answer about an allergy question asked earlier.
quests.explanation: When you ask about a child's allergy, wait for the kitchen's answer before ordering - the order follows the reply, and the restaurant's statement isn't a guarantee.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: My mother can't eat spicy food, so please make hers the mild version. Mine's the regular, and we'll share the rice.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular Chicken Curry, Rice, Mild Chicken Curry
quests.hint: Two versions of one dish, plus one shared side.
quests.explanation: Explaining a limit like 'can't eat spicy food' quickly tells the server which version to bring, without a long conversation.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the guest's final order.
quests.prompt: Hold on - she's just told me she wants the salmon instead of the chicken. Sorry. And I'll keep my soup.
quests.hint: The change comes from another person, relayed by the speaker.
quests.explanation: Passing on a friend's change of mind ('she's just told me...') works like any correction - the replaced item is dropped.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the guest's final order.
quests.prompt: My husband's shaking his head - he doesn't want the fries after all, he'd rather have the rice. My burger stays the same.
quests.hint: A gesture and a reported preference change one side dish.
quests.explanation: You can report someone's change of mind even from body language, as long as you say clearly what replaces the old item.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the guest's final order.
quests.prompt: Server: So that's two pastas and a pizza? Customer: Actually, my friend just said she'd prefer the pizza, so one pasta and two pizzas.
quests.hint: The counts change while the dishes stay the same.
quests.explanation: When a friend switches, the quantities move but the menu items don't - so the tapped items stay the same as before.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Right, for the six of us: two margherita pizzas, one with extra basil, a large salad to share, and the kids will have the pasta, plain, no sauce.
quests.correctAnswer: Kids' Pasta, Large Salad, Margherita Pizza
quests.hint: Two pizzas share one base item, and the kids' dish is described by what it lacks.
quests.explanation: This level combines a repeated item, a shared dish, and a plain version for the kids - the skills of the unit in one order.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Server: Ready for the table? Customer: Almost - my brother's vegan, so he'll have the vegetable curry, my mum will have the fish with rice, and I'll have the same as her but with chips instead of rice.
quests.correctAnswer: Fish with Chips, Vegetable Curry, Fish with Rice
quests.hint: One diner's order is defined by copying another's and changing one part.
quests.explanation: The last person's order builds on the previous one - 'the same as her but with chips' produces a third distinct item.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the guest's final order.
quests.prompt: It's my parents' anniversary: Dad's having the steak, medium, Mum's having the sea bass but she'd like salad instead of potatoes, and I'll have the risotto.
quests.hint: A swap in one person's plate means one side isn't ordered.
quests.explanation: 'Salad instead of potatoes' removes the potatoes from the order, so they shouldn't be tapped even though they're mentioned.
